newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: INTERVIEW - Bangladesh Bank chief dispells fears.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Bangladesh Bank chief dispells fears.

text.p: The head of Bangladesh's central bank said on Sunday the country's economy was in good health and did not face any danger from a recent crisis over commercial banks' inability to recover a huge backlog of bad debt.
Lutfar Rahman Sarkar, governor of Bangladesh Bank, said stringent legal and administrative measures were being implemented to streamline lending and recovery.
"A task force has been formed in the central bank to monitor progress (of loan recovery,)" he told Reuters in an interview.
"The worthiness of the borrowers would (henceforth) be examined carefully along with the viability of projects (they want to finance) before approval of credit," he said.
Besides, each bank had already created their own monitoring cells for strong supervision of loan recovery.
A bank reforms commission, which includes the governor himself, has advised the government to form a "consortium of commercial banks for giving credit to big projects".
The commission also proposed that a loan court be set up in each of Bangladesh's 64 administrative districts for quick disposal of some 50,000 cases now pending, Sarkar said.

He outlined the measures five days after a central bank news release quoted Sarkar as telling a meeting of legal advisers of commericial banks that the country's banking system was on the verge of collapse.
This had triggered an alarm and many banks immediately reined in their lending.
Sarkar on Sunday appeared to be trying to tone down his earlier warning by saying that the news release quoted him in stronger words than he had actually used.
He, however, did not deny that the banking sector was shambles over defaulted loans.
The governor earlier said private and public commercial banks had 130 billion taka ($3 billion) in oustanding loans, which could not be recovered mainly because of insufficient laws.
Banking sources said the rate of default on credit from private banks was 48 percent, from public banks 35 percent and from development financial institutions up to 90 percent.
Sarkar said on Sunday that despite a vigorous drive for realising the loans only 15 billion taka had been recovered so far.
"We could not do much so far for inadequacy of the legal framework. Till end of March (from January) we realised 15 billion taka," Sarkar said.
"The achievement (in credit recovery) is not quite unsatisfactory," he added.
The loan recovery was expected to improve when a bankruptcy law passed by parliament earlier this year would take effect and new legal procedures be introduced, the governor said without elaborating.
The central bank chief painted a rosy picture of Bangladesh's economy.

"The economy is in good shape. Inflation rate is only 3.2 percent. The (present) growth rate is more than 5.0 percent while the (annual) target (for fiscal 1996/97 July-June) is 5.5 percent," he said.
He described the import situation as "quite satisfactory". Imports had grown by eight percent over last eight months against export growth of 7.8 percent, he said.
